title: Fix install.sh so a new terminal finds forgel-code on PATH
request: The installer currently completes while the launcher directory never reaches PATH in a freshly opened terminal. It picks the profile file from $SHELL alone: on macOS a bash login shell never reads ~/.bashrc, and under `curl … | sh` $SHELL can be empty, sending the block to ~/.profile while the terminal reads ~/.zshrc. It also never checks that its own change took effect. This change makes the installer detect the real login shell, write the block into a profile file a new terminal actually reads, start a clean login shell afterwards and verify that `forgel-code` resolves, and fail with a message naming the edited file and the observed PATH when it does not. --uninstall removes the block from every profile file the installer can have written.

audit.summary: The release meets the main install.sh PATH requirements and the final suite passes, but the bounded fresh-shell verification is unsafe and incomplete: the checked shell is never placed in its own process group, the root is reaped before the grace-period KILL, and the cleanup can leave reparented descendants or signal a recycled PID. This violates the bounded-check cleanup contract and can affect unrelated processes. Two smaller evidence/edge-case gaps are also present.

findings.issue: `bounded_run` starts the checked login shell in the installer's own process group. Because `signal_run` compares the checked process's pgid with `$$`, it always falls back to `process_tree` and never signals a dedicated group. At timeout the watcher sends TERM, then waits `VERIFY_GRACE` before KILL, while the main path's `wait "$child"` reaps the root immediately. Descendants that outlive the root are reparented and disappear from the process tree, so they can survive the cleanup; the delayed KILL also targets an already-reaped PID, which can be reused and cause an unrelated process or process group to be killed.
findings.suggestion: Run the checked command in a private process group and signal that group, or keep the root unreaped until the watcher finishes and verify PID identity/start time before any delayed kill. Ensure cleanup also covers descendants that have been reparented after the root exits.

findings.issue: `remove_profile_block` identifies the installer's `MARKER_SEPARATOR` solely by line content and end-of-file position. If a user's file ends with that exact comment and a final newline, the uninstall removes the user's line. If content follows the block, the separator can be left behind instead of being removed.
findings.suggestion: Record the separator's presence with a distinct, non-user-reproducible marker or encode the original trailing-newline state in the block itself, so removal never infers it from ordinary line content.

findings.issue: Task 7 requirement R10/AC8 calls for measured before/after per-module or per-test durations. The review states those numbers were not in its context, so the speedup diagnosis is not evidenced in the provided audit artifacts.
findings.suggestion: Attach or record the measured before/after durations in the task report so the runtime reduction is verified rather than inferred.
